signals.title: JPY — BoJ Split + Options Skew + ESI
signals.text: The BoJ Summary of Opinions from the July meeting reveals a significant board split regarding the pace of normalization, with some members advocating for nimble rate adjustments to counter upside inflation risks. USD/JPY trades at 158.04, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (161.24/161.17/158.07), signaling a breakdown in medium-term technical support. Options markets show high conviction in further downside with a USD/JPY 25d Risk Reversal of -2.20, representing a strong put skew for the base currency. This aligns with a positive JPY Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +17.2, as Japanese data continues to outperform expectations. While the 267bp Fed-BoJ OIS carry differential remains a structural hurdle for JPY bulls, the hawkish internal BoJ dialogue forces a repricing of the hiking path. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; hawkish BoJ shift and technical breakdown target further downside. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hold priced. Risk: US CPI surprise re-establishes USD yield dominance, stalling the JPY recovery.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT-OIS Divergence + RBNZ
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5886, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following a period of sustained data outperformance. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. The New Zealand Economic Surprise Index (ESI) leads the G10 at +24.4, directly contradicting the crowded spec short. Retail sentiment adds a contrarian layer with 76% of retail traders short, increasing the risk of a sharp short-squeeze if upcoming data remains robust. The 125bp Fed-RBNZ OIS carry advantage for the USD is being challenged by this asymmetric positioning setup. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD; asymmetric short-squeeze risk against crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike priced. Risk: global risk-off sentiment triggers a flight to USD, validating the existing spec short.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Carry
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3487, remaining technically well-supported above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3412/1.3366/1.3406). The options market is pricing an elevated Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of +4.9 points, with IV at 11.0% vs HV30 of 6.1%, signaling significant demand for protection despite relatively calm realized volatility. COT positioning shows speculative net longs at +39,039 (70.1% long), indicating a market that remains structurally long Cable but is paying up for downside hedges. The carry environment is neutral with a -8bp OIS differential between the Fed and BoE, leaving price action dependent on idiosyncratic UK data. Real policy rates favor GBP at +0.93% vs USD +1.56%, keeping the spread relatively tight in a low-volatility regime (VIX 14.9). Trade bias: Neutral/Bullish GBP/USD; technical support holds while vol premium signals cautious long positioning. Catalyst: UK employment data. Risk: VRP collapses on a realized vol spike, forcing a liquidation of stale longs.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Options-Positioning Alignment
signals.text: EUR/USD sits at 1.1558, trading above its SMA20/50 cluster but capped below the SMA200 at 1.1633. Speculative positioning remains net short (LF net -73,049, long% 34%), which aligns with a 135bp OIS carry advantage favoring the USD. The options market confirms this bearish bias with a mild put skew in 25d Risk Reversals at -0.37. Despite recent Euro futures strength noted by CME Group research, the real rate differential remains thin (+0.13% for EUR vs +1.56% for USD), providing little structural support for a sustained breakout. Elevated VRP of +2.7% (IV 7.1% vs HV30 4.4%) suggests that while the trend has been marginally higher, participants are actively hedging against a reversal. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD; carry disadvantage and SMA200 resistance cap upside potential. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — hike priced. Risk: US inflation data misses, narrowing the real rate gap and forcing a cover of the spec short.
